title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
abstract: arXiv:2611.34106v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Symbolic regression seeks to discover interpretable governing equations for dynamical systems from data. In systems biology, however, accurately reproducing system trajectories does not necessarily imply recovery of the underlying reaction mechanisms. Existing benchmarks evaluate numerical accuracy, expression complexity, or equation-level similarity, but not agreement between recovered reactions and reference mechanisms in biological systems. We introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems with reaction annotations spanning mass action, Michaelis--Menten, Hill, and complex kinetics. Trajectory fidelity is evaluated across all systems under in-distribution reconstruction and out-of-distribution (OOD) extrapolation, while mechanism recovery is assessed on the subset of 161 systems. We evaluate trajectory fidelity across 11 symbolic-discovery methods and assess mechanism recovery for three reaction-base

tldr: 本文提出SysBio-SR基准，包含198个带反应注释的生物ODE系统，首次系统评估符号回归方法在轨迹保真度与机制恢复两个维度上的表现，揭示了准确拟合系统轨迹并不等于恢复真实的生物反应机制。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 annotated biological ODE systems that systematically evaluates symbolic regression methods on both trajectory fidelity and mechanism recovery, revealing that accurately reproducing system trajectories does not necessarily imply recovery of the underlying biological reaction mechanisms.
